goal: Every role session is told what it is, and what it was told can be checked afterwards. A role file is the only instruction a headless session gets, so an edit to one has to be demonstrable — not believed.

Neither is true today. `canon/roles/plan.md` is six lines and every one of them is frontmatter: an `mc plan <programme>` session is told its model and nothing else beyond the shared `_common.md`, while every other role has a body (brief 111 lines, _common 68, step 55, intake 42, repair 38, helper 20, worker 16). This is on the record as unfinished — #580's subject is *"Every role says a turn is the cost; the plan role gets a body"*, and only the first half landed. It matters more after ruling 11 (2026-09-06), because there are now two roles that write plans and only one of them is told how.

And what a session runs on cannot be checked at all. This brief's own role text contains two sentences — *"A recommendation you cannot…"* and *"mc counts them and does…"* — that `canon/roles/brief.md` has not contained since #614 landed on 2026-09-05T12:18+02:00, a day before the session started; `git log -S` over both phrases finds them removed by that commit and by no other. `mc brief` reads `readCanonRole('brief')` and passes `role.overlay` through `instructionsFor` to `--append-system-prompt` (`src/mc/commands/brief.js:43`, `src/mc/roles.js`, `src/mc/portrait.js:103`), and nothing anywhere records what came out. So a session cannot answer *which revision of my role am I running*, and neither can anyone looking at it.
contract: **One door stays one door.** `instructionsFor(toolId, profile, overlay)` in `src/mc/roles.js` is where a session's instructions are assembled, for all four launch paths. Nothing here adds a second channel; what is recorded is recorded at that door or at the callers that already write a register.

**`_common.md` is not folded into `overlay`.** `run.js` tests `role.overlay` to decide whether a role file is installed at all, and a shared preamble folded in ahead of that check would make a missing role look present — a headless session launched with no instructions for what it is doing. The reason is in `roles.js` § `SHARED_ROLE_FILE` and it stands.

**Canon roles stay repository-owned**, versioned with the code that launches them, and the user catalogue (`MC_ROLES_DIR`, else `<mc home>/roles`) keeps its precedence for roles that are not mc's own.

**`plan.md` restates nothing it does not own.** What a plan is, who may write one and what a session may not touch are settled in `docs/project/README.md` § *Who writes what*, in `src/mc/plan-schema.js` and in ruling 11 — the role points at them and does not fork them.
**No new session kind and no change to what mc launches.** This is about what a session is told and what is recorded about it.
out_of_scope: The other six role files' contents. `plan.md` is the one with no body; reading the rest against what they say today was #614's work and is not reopened here.

Rewriting `canon/roles/_common.md`. If a passage turns out to belong to every role rather than to the two that write plans, that is a finding for a later step to raise, not a licence to edit the shared file in this one.

Finding out what produced this brief's stale text. The project makes the divergence visible and checkable; chasing one instance of it through a launcher that has already exited is not something a plan can promise.

What a planning session is *for*. Ruling 11 settled the split — the brief writes the plans it decides, the planning session thinks a programme through and reads a `plan-review` — and this project writes that down rather than moving it.
`mc roles`' other sub-verbs and the user catalogue's own commands.

success_criteria.criterion: `canon/roles/plan.md` has an overlay body, and no canon role can ship without one again.
success_criteria.check: `readCanonRole('plan').overlay` is a non-empty string, and a test walks `canonRolesDir()` asserting every `*.md` that is not `_common.md` parses to a role with a non-null `overlay`. The test fails on today's tree.

success_criteria.criterion: The rules two roles now share about writing a plan are written once, and neither role file carries a second copy of them.
success_criteria.check: The shared passage lives in exactly one file; a test asserts the sentences that define it appear in one canon file and not in `plan.md` and `brief.md` both.

success_criteria.criterion: A live session records which role text it was launched with, and the record survives the launcher.
success_criteria.check: `~/mc/runner/foreground/<pid>.json` and `~/mc/runner/current-<repo>.json` carry the role name and a digest of the instructions `instructionsFor` returned; a test drives a launch with a fixture role and asserts the digest matches what that role's text hashes to.

success_criteria.criterion: A person can see, for any live session, whether the role text it is running on is the one on disk today.
success_criteria.check: One verb prints the instructions a launch would produce for a role and compares them with the digests the register holds, naming any session whose text is not canon's. Run against a session launched from a deliberately older role file, it names it; against a fresh one, it says nothing.

documents.label: Who writes what, and citing a decision
The plan file's schema and its frozen fields
mc: the rulings — ruling 11, the brief writes the plans it decides

steps.title: `canon/roles/plan.md` gets a body, and the plan-writing rules are written once
steps.done_when: `canon/roles/plan.md` has an overlay that tells a planning session what it is for and how a plan is written; the rules it shares with `canon/roles/brief.md` exist in one file that both inherit; and a test asserts every canon role but `_common.md` has a non-null overlay.
instruction: `canon/roles/plan.md` is six lines — `name`, `model`, `singleton`, `tools` — and no body at all. `readCanonRole('plan').overlay` is `null`, so an `mc plan <programme>` session is told `_common.md` and its profile and nothing about planning. Every other role has a body. #580 was called *"Every role says a turn is the cost; the plan role gets a body"* and delivered only the first half; ruling 6 in `docs/project/mc/rulings.md` records that the model on that file had never been placed deliberately either.

Write the body out of what is already settled rather than inventing a doctrine. `docs/project/README.md` § *Who writes what* says a planning session opens on a programme and not on a project, that it lives at `~/mc/plan/<programme>/` with no workarea, that what it shares with the runner is a `PLAN.json` on `main` and nothing else, and that the `<project>` directory name becomes the branch and the workarea. `src/mc/plan-schema.js` is the shape: `goal`, `contract`, `out_of_scope`, `success_criteria` with a `check` on each, `documents`, `runner`, and one entry per step carrying that step's own instruction and state — plus `PLAN_FROZEN_FIELDS`, which is what a step session may never touch. § *Citing a decision* says where a ruling goes and how a decision is quoted rather than pathed.

Say what a planning session is for now that it is not the only thing that writes plans. Ruling 11 (2026-09-06) gave the brief the plans it decides; what stays here is thinking a programme through — how many projects come out of it, under what names, in what order — and reading a plan a step has asked a `plan-review` of. A brief that has just read the code and taken Martin's GO does not hand that to a second session, and a planning session does not take work the brief has already decided.

The overlap with `brief.md` is now real: both write plans, both consume proposals, both land through a pull request. Write those sentences **once**. `_common.md` is the file every role inherits and it is not the right home — this is shared by two roles, not by all eight, and folding it there would tell a `step` session how to write a plan it may not write. So make it a passage of its own that both role files carry by reference, or split the shared half into a file the two of them include; whichever you choose, `instructionsFor` assembles profile, `_common.md` and the overlay in that order and the mechanism for a third piece has to go through that same door. Do not fold anything into `overlay` before `run.js`'s `role.overlay` check — `roles.js` § `SHARED_ROLE_FILE` says why, and that reason still holds.

Then the guard that stops this happening again: a test over `canonRolesDir()` asserting every `*.md` that is not `_common.md` parses to a role whose `overlay` is a non-empty string. It fails on today's tree, which is the point of writing it first.

steps.title: A session records the role text it was given, and a verb says whether it is canon's
steps.done_when: Every launched session's register entry carries its role name and a digest of the instructions it was given, and one verb prints what a launch would produce for a role today and names any live session whose recorded digest is not that.
instruction: The fault this step closes, stated exactly: this brief's running role text contains *"A recommendation you cannot…"* and *"mc counts them and does…"*, two sentences `git log -S` shows were removed from `canon/roles/brief.md` by #614 on 2026-09-05T12:18+02:00 — a day before the session started. So the text a session runs on can differ from the file on disk. **Do not try to reconstruct why that particular session's text was old**; the launcher has exited and the answer is not recoverable. What is fixable is that nobody could have noticed at all.

`instructionsFor(toolId, profile, overlay)` in `src/mc/roles.js` is the single door — four launch paths go through it (`work-open.js` twice, `run.js`, `helper-turn.js`). Nothing records what it returned. Two registers already exist and are written at launch: `~/mc/runner/foreground/<pid>.json` (verb, area, tool, model, pid, started) and `~/mc/runner/current-<repo>.json` (name, kind, repo, lane, tool, model, budget, pid, worktree). Add the role name and a digest of the assembled instructions to whichever of them each path writes — a short hash, not the text: the register is read by the page and by `mc status`, and a 5 kB overlay in a file the page parses every draw is a cost for nothing.

Then one verb that answers the question. `mc roles show <name>` prints a role's own words from disk today; give it — or a sibling — the assembled form, exactly what `instructionsFor` would return for that role and tool, so the two halves of the comparison are the same object. And have it name any live session in the registers whose recorded digest is not the one canon hashes to now. That is the whole feature: *this session is running a role text that is not the one on disk*, said out loud, by name.

A session whose role legitimately came from the user catalogue rather than canon is not a fault and must not be reported as one — `areaRole` prefers `readRole` (the catalogue) over `readCanonRole` on purpose. Record which source the text came from beside the digest so the comparison knows what it is comparing against.

Test it by driving a launch with a fixture role directory, asserting the digest the register receives is the hash of profile + `_common.md` + that role's overlay joined the way `instructionsFor` joins them; then change the fixture file and assert the verb names the session. Do not assert on a real running session — the test must not depend on what happens to be open on this machine.

Where the answer belongs on the page is not this step's to decide. `mc status <name>` is the surface that already reports one session whole, and a drift line there is the smallest honest place for it; the page's own section order is `the-page-remade`'s and is not touched here.
